Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution o  issuance of a Writ of Mandamus, directing the 1st respondent to gra  enhanced compensation at Rs.7/- per sq. feet for acquiring the subj  properties situated at Erode Taluk, Erode District in accordance to  of this Court in Review Application Nos.40, 41, 42 of 2007 dated 29
and by considering the petitioner's representation dated 11.08.2023

For Petitioners : Mr. M. Guruprasad  For Respondents 1 & 4 : Mr. C. Jayaprakash,
 Government Advocate  For Respondents 2, 3 & 5 : Mr. C. Kalaichelvan  Standing Counsel  ORDER

The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the first respondent to grant the enhanced compensation at Rs.7/- per sq. feet for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis acquiring the subject properties situated at Erode Taluk, Erode District, in accordance to the order of this Court in Review Application Nos.40, 41, 42 of 2007 dated 29.07.2013, by considering the petitioners'
representation dated 11.08.2023.

2. Learned standing counsel appearing on behalf of the Tamil Nadu Housing Board made a submission that pursuant to the Award passed in the Land Acquisition Proceedings, compensation has been deposited in the Court.
It is not in dispute that section 18 reference was made and the LAOP Court enhanced the compensation from Rs.1 to Rs.7 per sq. ft.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation as determined by the Court on par with other erstwhile land owners.

3. In the present case, the learned standing counsel appearing on behalf of the Tamil Nadu Housing Board made a submission that the Board is ready to settle the compensation and there was a dispute between the legal heirs of the erstwhile owner.

In this context, the learned counsel for the P. Mathiyazhagan S/O. M. Ponnusamy vs The Revenue Divisional Officer on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6409287/
2 petitioners made a submission that there is no dispute as such amongst the legal heirs and the petitioners have already produced the records.

sentences.text: That being the case, the Board is now submitting incorrect facts in order to cover-up the delay committed by them.

5. May that as it be, the petitioners are at liberty to submit the death certificate and legal heir certificate of the original claimant, before the competent authority of the Tamil Nadu Housing Board.

On such submission, the competent authority is directed to settle the enhanced amount of compensation along with the interest and other permissible benefits under the Land Acquisition Act in favour of the writ petitioners within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the death certificate and legal heir certificate from the petitioners.
6. With the above direction, the writ petition stands allowed.
